misconceptions.description: Building personas from demographics (age, job title) instead of from goals, constraints, and contexts that would actually stress the design
misconceptions.trigger: persona reads '34-year-old manager' with no goal, barrier, or access condition that the prototype must serve
misconceptions.feedback: A simulation-useful persona names a goal, a constraint, and a context of use, not just demographics. Otherwise it cannot reveal a failure.

misconceptions.description: Running every persona down the ideal path so the simulation never encounters an error, interruption, or unsupported branch
misconceptions.trigger: all persona walkthroughs succeed on the first try with no friction logged
misconceptions.feedback: Drive at least one persona into an interruption, wrong turn, or low-bandwidth condition. A check that never fails has tested nothing.

misconceptions.description: Recording a persona walkthrough observation but never converting it into a specific change to the prototype
misconceptions.trigger: simulation notes list problems but the prototype is unchanged afterward
misconceptions.feedback: Pair each persona finding with the exact screen or step you will revise, or a justified decision not to.

misconceptions.description: Treating an AI role-playing a persona as equivalent to a real user test and reporting its reactions as user data
misconceptions.trigger: learner cites 'the AI persona said the navigation was confusing' as a usability finding
misconceptions.feedback: An AI persona can generate candidate failure modes to check, but its reactions are hypotheses, not user data. Verify against the design and, where possible, a real user.
